For the text || South Africa's trip to Kanpur for the third test against India has given former England test cricketer Bob Woolmer the chance of a sentimental return to his birthplace. || extract entities using the order: left to right

For the text || Woolmer was born in the northern city of Kanpur when his father worked there for an insurance compnay and was himself an active cricketer. || extract entities using the order: left to right
For the text || "It's been a sentimental journey ... || extract entities using the order: left to right
For the text || A visit to India is always an intriguing experience, "Woolmer, now the South African coach, said on Saturday. || extract entities using the order: left to right

For the text || His first cricketing sojurn to India was as a member of Tony Greig's England side in 1976-77. || extract entities using the order: left to right

For the text || His father Clarence Woolmer represented United Province, now renamed Uttar Pradesh, in India's Ranji Trophy national championship and captained the state during 1949. || extract entities using the order: left to right
For the text || Now aged 86, Woolmer senior lives with his son in Cape Town. || extract entities using the order: left to right
For the text || Woolmer's memories of Kanpur are few and blurred. || extract entities using the order: left to right
For the text || "I don't remember much of the place," he said. " || extract entities using the order: left to right

For the text || I came here on zero and left at three (aged three) when my father was transferred to Calcutta where I spent another four and half years. || extract entities using the order: left to right
